title.narrative: Technorseve -Stöd till utveckling inom förädlingsindustrin för jordbruk
Technoserve- Support to the agroprocessing industry

description.narrative:
Det övergripande målet för FED-projektet är att öka intäkterna och säljbara volymer, samt skapa och/eller behålla jobb för minst 100 små och medelstora företag inom livsmedelstillverkning, varav minst 50 % av dessa företag kommer att ägas av kvinnor. Detta kommer att ske via tre sammankopplade aktiviteter, nämligen:
1) utföra sektorövergripande utbildningar för utvalda små och medelstora företag; 2) erbjuda skräddarsydda affärsplaner och teknisk assistans för utvalda små och medelstora företag; samt 3) förbättra tillgången till finansiering för utvalda små och medelstora företag.
När dessa aktiviteter kombineras så kan effektiviteten, lönsamheten och tillväxten hos små och medelstora företag nom livsmedelsindustri förbättras vilket bidrar till en starkare och mer inkluderande sektor. Preliminärt har TechnoServe visat att de kommer att arbeta med små och medelstora företag som främst kommer från Lusaka, Kopparbältet, centrala samt östra provinserna. Aktiviteter specifikt inom majs- och kassavasektorn kommer att ske i nordvästra och södra provinserna. Det faktiska geografiska verksamhetsområdet kommer att bestämmas under inledningsfasen på sex månader.
Avtalspartnern är TechnoServe som är en ideell internationell utvecklingsorganisation med sitt huvudkontor i USA och ett landskontor i Zambia.
Budgeten för den föreslagna insatsen är 36 miljoner kronor. Projektet kommer att pågå i tre och ett halvt år (42 månader), inklusive en inledningsfas på sex månader. Det kommer inte att vidarebefordras medel till tredje part.

The overall goal of the FED project is to increase revenues and marketable volumes and create or retain jobs for 100 SME enterprises, 50% of which will be women owned. This will be done via three inter-linked activities namely:
1) delivering sector wide trainings (SWTs) to selected SMEs; 2) providing customised business and technical assistance for selected SMEs; and 3) improving access to finance for selected SMEs.
When combined, these activities improve the efficiency, profitability and growth of food processing SMEs and contribute to a stronger and more inclusive sector. Tentatively TechnoServe has indicated that it will work with SMEs that are primarily from Lusaka, Central, Copperbelt and Eastern provinces. However, assessment of clusters of maize and cassava processors in North-Western and Southern (Livingstone) provinces will also be considered. The actual geographical area of operation will be decided during the inception period of 6 months.
The agreement partner is TechnoServe is a not-for-profit international development organization with its headquarters in the USA and a country office in Zambia.
The budget for the proposed intervention is SEK 36Million. The project will run for three and a half years (42 months), including an inception phase of six months. There will be no forwarding of funds to third parties.

The FED Project aims to increase the revenues, marketable output and job security for more than 100 SMEs within Zambias food processing sector. Furthermore, the contribution intends to deepen the SMEs capacity and sustainability, equipping them with technical and business skills in food processing best practices, and improving their access to inputs, new markets and finance through inclusive models. The three specific objectives that will support the overall project goal of A more inclusive SME food processing sector resulting in increased resilience and economic and nutritional benefits for the Bottom of the Pyramid (BOP) particularly women and youth are: 1) Improving sustainability the productivity and profitability of the SMEs/SGBs food processors. 2) Improving the performance of women led or owned food processors SMEs/ SGBs. 3) Improving the market systems service providers capacity to support SME/ SGBs food processors.

title.narrative: Decision on Amendment of Contribution Technoserve Support to Agro-Processing Dec 2020

description.narrative:
- Technoserve (TNS) managed to onboard a second cohort of 64 SMEs in year two of project making the total number of businesses that are supported to 103. All these businesses (103 out of the target 100) continued to receive Customised Training Assistance (CTA) and Sector Wide Trainings (SWT). - TNS managed to conducted two SWT that targeted all the TNS supported SMEs and other businesses outside the project.
The first sector-wide training focused on horticultural training which attracted 363 participants, mostly farmers (152 females). The aim of this training was to teach the farmers on how to grow the horticultural crops tomatoes, rape, cabbages etc) for onwards supply to the formal markets.
The second SWT was on food laws in Zambia. It attracted twenty five (25) small and medium business enterprises (13 female led/owned businesses ). This training was facilitated by TNS but the main presenters during the training were officials from regulating institutions i.e. officials from Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of Local Government (MLG), National Food Laboratory, the Zambia Compulsory Standards Agency (ZCSA), The Zambia Bureau of Standards (ZBS), and the Zambia Metrology Agency (ZMA). The aim of this training was to improve awareness, perception and understanding of food regulations in Zambia which will lead to increased adherence.
- TNS managed to link the businesses it is working with to Financial Institutions (FIs) for additional financial support. During this reporting period, 13 businesses have received external financing from FIs amounting to over ZMW4,300,000.
- 17 out of the 38 clients (from cohort one) recorded an increased revenue, while 14 out of the 38 showed an increase in their production. The rest of the businesses (21 out of 38) had challenges in improving their businesses in terms of production and revenue due to various reasons. Some of the challenges were for example high cost of doing business (e.g high costs for various permits required to be paid which impacted on their capital), governance issues within their businesses, failure to find new markets for their products etc. TNS has not abandoned this category of businesses facing challenges. TNS has continued providing CTA and linking them to other stakeholders who could help.
- Due to improved performance of the enterprises engaged by TNS, 105 new jobs were reportedly created. In addition, over 1400 individuals (739 women) were indirectly supported by the project through raw material supply to the TNS supported businesses.
-10 companies were coached to attain certification with a combination of lower and higher certification. Out of these, 7 were for local supplier or permit to supply locally while the 3 were for higher level certification. Higher certification include the Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) and Food Safety System Certification Scheme (FSSC). Such higher level certification enables businesses to access export markets, in this case the EU and United States markets. - 32 businesses (13 women owned/led) were able to penetrate new markets after receiving CTA. This resulted in a cumulative total of 51 out of the target 75 businesses being able to access formal markets.
- TNS continued to hold stakeholders meetings with the aim of improving on outreach, advocacy and market access of FED project activities. These stakeholders included the businesses associations, private sector institutions, the public and individuals. TNS has continued to sign MoUs and currently has 4 with Prospero, Zambia Development Agency (ZDA), Zambia Cooperative Federation (ZCF), Zambia Bureau of Standards (ZBS).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
